hints.title: Edge Alignment Minimizes Brick Cuts
hints.text: A vertical cut that passes through a brick edge cuts zero bricks at that row. More aligned edges means fewer cuts.

hints.title: Prefix Edge Frequency Tracking
hints.text: Calculate cumulative brick edge positions for each row, excluding the final right boundary. Track the frequency of each edge coordinate.

hints.title: Total Rows Minus Most Frequent Edge
hints.text: Traverse each row, accumulating prefix width up to the second-to-last brick and tallying edge positions. The answer is total rows minus the maximum edge frequency.

hints.title: See the blueprint

variables: N: total number of bricks across all rows
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N) time and O(W) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing every integer position from 1 to total width takes O(Width * Rows), which times out for large widths up to 2^31.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Hashing only actual existing edge locations reduces work strictly to the total number of bricks N.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should avoid counting the outer right boundary to ensure the cut stays strictly inside the wall.
